text:
maya: Hey folks — I need to swap my Sun 10:00–18:00 oncall block. Family wedding out of town, flight arrives late Sat. I can do a full handoff and leave prewarm scripts + a short checklist. Would anyone be able to pick this up? :bouquet:

alex: I can take it if that helps. Are there any expected deploys or maintenance windows during that slot?

maya: Thanks Alex! No planned deploys AFAIK. Main things to watch: prewarm the LLM KV cache for the chat-models, ensure batcher config doesn't drop to aggressive batching during low traffic, and the nightly backup job for embeddings runs at 02:30 UTC (not in your slot but FYI).

juan: I can shadow the first hour just to get context if you want a pair handoff.

maya: That'd be great, Juan — appreciate it. I'll walk through everything tomorrow morning in a short async note. Quick checklist I will leave in the handoff: 
- creds: seat-specific token is revoked, use the oncall API token in LastPass (path: /redwood/oncall/api).
- runbook pointers: /runbooks/oncall/early-warning and /runbooks/oncall/cache-warmup.
- prewarm scripts: run `scripts/prewarm_kv_cache.sh --models chat-* --parallel=4` (should finish ~4–6min).
- warmup queries: sample prompts in `handoff/warmup_prompts.txt` — try first two for latency smoke test.
- canary: if you need to roll, prefer canary on dedicated pool (policy `canary-small`) and watch latency metrics for 20 min before full.

sophie: Where will you post the handoff note? Slack or ops docs?

maya: I'll paste the full handoff into this thread and also push to the oncall-docs page (link in the note). I'll attach the warmup script output and small perf snapshot.

ops-bot: deploybot noticed: No scheduled deploys during 2026-08-23 10:00–18:00 UTC.

alex: OK taking it. Juan, can you shadow 10:00–11:00 with me?

juan: Yep I'll be available. Send me the quick commands you want me to run during the handoff.

maya: Quick run-through commands (I will paste into the doc too):
```bash
# check model pool health
redwoodctl pool status --pool dedicated-chat
# quick latency smoke (10 requests)
for i in {1..10}; do redwoodctl invoke --model chat-small --prompt "hello"; done
# check batcher queue length
redwoodctl metrics get batcher.queue_length --last 5m
```

maya: If the prewarm script fails or times out, fallback is: restart the prewarm with `--parallel=2`, then run a single warmup prompt against each model variant. If latency spikes >200ms p50 after warmup, promote canary rollback and ping infra oncall.

alex: Got it. Two quick Qs: 1) Do we need to bump token limits for warmup? 2) Any customers on planned experiments that might cause traffic blips?

maya: 1) The script uses the oncall token and is scoped; no limit bump needed. It uses small prompts. 2) There is a low-risk A/B from marketing that could spike embeddings usage briefly (~10 rps) starting Sun 15:00 UTC; I left a note with the product owner and it's unlikely to affect p99 but worth watching embeddings throughput.

juan: I'll set an alert on the embeddings ingest metric for +20% increase during Alex's window.

alex: I'll accept the swap in the schedule and post a 10:00 quick-check message in #eng-oncall when I start. Anything else to be aware of?

maya: That's it from me — I also added a short manual rollback snippet if the canary shows issues: `redwoodctl rollout rollback --to previous --pool dedicated-chat`.

ops-bot: reminder: oncall handbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/oncall-handbook

alex: Thanks Maya — enjoy the wedding and safe travels! :tada:

maya: Appreciate it. I'll DM the travel ETA and attach the final handoff in this thread before I leave.
